q: Polki or diamond jewellery: what should I wear for the wedding, reception and sangeet?
a: A simple plan works well: Polki for the wedding ceremony with a heavy bridal lehenga, diamond jewellery for the reception in a lighter outfit, and lighter Polki or diamond pieces for the sangeet and mehendi. Choose one hero necklace per function so the looks feel different. We help brides plan every function at our Parle Point showroom or on a video call - WhatsApp +91 99980 43886.

q: How do I match jewellery to a heavily embroidered lehenga without overdoing it?
a: Pick one hero piece, usually the necklace, and keep the rest in proportion. Echo one stone colour from the embroidery, keep earrings lighter if the neckline is busy, and skip extra layers where the work is heaviest. Bring a photo of your lehenga to our showroom and we will try pieces against it with you.

q: What jewellery does a bride need from the wedding day to the reception?
a: Most brides plan a main necklace set with earrings, a maang tikka or matha patti, bangles or kadas, rings and a nath for the wedding, then a lighter necklace or choker with earrings for the reception and smaller sets for the sangeet and mehendi. Make a list function by function and see which pieces can be worn twice. Custom bridal pieces from our own manufacturing unit usually take 2 to 4 weeks, so plan early.

q: What jewellery suits a velvet, emerald, wine or navy lehenga for a winter wedding?
a: Rich jewel tones look best with warm gold, Polki and uncut diamonds, or emeralds and pearls that pick up the colour of the outfit. Keep one strong necklace and let the velvet stay the backdrop. You can see Polki and diamond sets against your own outfit colour at our showroom in Parle Point, Surat.

q: Which statement piece should I wear with a plain or minimal organza lehenga?
a: Choose one focal piece, such as a Polki choker, a diamond necklace or a pair of statement earrings, and keep everything else light. A minimal outfit lets a single piece stand out, so pick the one that suits your neckline. We can show you options from our collection or make one to order.

q: How do I get a layered royal bridal look with Polki, emeralds and pearls without it looking too heavy?
a: Build the look in steps: a maang tikka or matha patti, one layered necklace instead of several separate ones, and kadas that match. Space the layers so each one shows, and ask for lighter construction so the set stays comfortable through long functions. Our own manufacturing unit can adjust weight, length and clasps to suit you.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a tissue or silk saree for my wedding reception?
a: A diamond or light Polki necklace with matching earrings suits a saree well, because the drape and pallu leave the neckline open. Keep the necklace length clear of the pallu and choose earrings that frame the face. These pieces can also be worn again at family functions after the wedding.

q: What jewellery suits a floral or multicolour embroidered lehenga in blush, mint or mehendi green?
a: Soft floral colours pair well with Polki, uncut diamonds, pearls or emeralds. Pick one hero piece and keep the colours of the stones close to one shade in the embroidery so the outfit stays the focus. We can help you match pieces to your lehenga photo in the showroom or on a video call.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a mirror-work or sequin lehenga for the sangeet or a night reception?
a: When the outfit already shines, choose fewer pieces with a clean shape: statement earrings or a structured diamond or Polki necklace rather than many layers. This keeps the look balanced under evening lights. Visit our Parle Point showroom to try options with your outfit photo.

q: Which maang tikka or matha patti suits my face shape and hairstyle?
a: A single drop tikka suits most faces and a centre parting; a matha patti works well with a broader forehead and a low bun; a passa on one side suits side partings and modern looks. Check the weight and the hook or clasp so it stays in place through the day. Try a few styles at our showroom to see what suits you.

q: What is the difference between CVD and HPHT lab-grown diamonds, and is the method on the report?
a: CVD and HPHT are the two main ways diamonds are grown in a laboratory: CVD builds the crystal layer by layer from a carbon gas, and HPHT recreates high pressure and temperature. Both produce real diamond. Grading reports for lab-grown diamonds state that the stone is laboratory-grown, and many also note the growth method and any post-growth treatment; read the report details, and we will go through yours with you.

q: Can I wear my diamond ring every day?
a: Yes, a well-set diamond ring can be worn daily. Take it off for the gym, heavy housework, swimming and when using chemicals or creams, and get the prongs checked once or twice a year. Bring your ring to our showroom and we will check the setting.

q: Which solitaire ring setting is best for daily wear and for long fingers or small hands?
a: For daily wear, a lower setting with sturdy prongs or a bezel catches less on clothes. Oval, pear and marquise shapes make fingers look longer, and a slimmer band suits small hands. Try several settings on your own hand at our showroom before you decide.

q: What jewellery looks best with an ivory or off-white lehenga?
a: Ivory is a clean base, so the jewellery can lead: Polki and uncut diamonds set in gold, pearls with emeralds, or a diamond choker with a long necklace. Add one colour through the stones if you want contrast. We can show you combinations from our Polki and diamond collection.

q: How do I style a necklace with a double dupatta or cape lehenga so the jewellery is still seen?
a: Choose a choker or a short necklace that sits above the drape, and keep a longer haar only if it can lie clear of the dupatta. Earrings and a maang tikka become more important because they frame the face. Our own manufacturing unit can adjust necklace lengths and clasps to suit your outfit.

q: Which jewellery goes with a sequin or crystal net lehenga without clashing?
a: Keep the jewellery soft and clean so it does not compete with the shine of the fabric: uncut or rose-cut diamonds, one hero necklace and slim earrings. Avoid many layers on a heavily embellished outfit. Try options against your outfit photo at our Parle Point showroom.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a gown or indo-western outfit for my engagement or cocktail night?
a: A diamond choker, a solitaire pendant or statement diamond earrings suit most gown necklines. Match the necklace to the neckline: chokers for strapless and off-shoulder, pendants for V-necks. Every piece we sell comes with its grading report and a BIS HUID hallmark on the gold.

q: What jewellery does a Gujarati bride wear with a panetar, gharchola or Banarasi saree?
a: A Gujarati bride often wears a rani haar or long necklace with a choker, a nath, a maang tikka or matha patti, earrings and bangles alongside her chudo. Polki and gold-set uncut diamond sets suit the red and white of the panetar and gharchola well. We make Polki and bridal sets in our own manufacturing unit in Surat - visit us at Parle Point or WhatsApp +91 99980 43886.

q: How do I choose kadas and bangles to wear with my chooda and bridal lehenga?
a: Keep the kadas in proportion to the chooda and the necklace: one or two strong kadas on each wrist balance a heavy set more easily than many thin ones. Match the metal and stones to your necklace. Each gold kada carries its own BIS HUID, which we show you against the bill.

q: Is a diamond certificate the same as a hallmark?
a: No. A diamond grading report from IGI, EGL or TGL describes the diamonds, while the BIS HUID hallmark confirms the purity of the gold. A good piece of diamond jewellery comes with both, and you can verify the HUID in the BIS Care app and the report number on the laboratory's website.

q: How do I know the stone I am buying is a diamond and not moissanite or a simulant?
a: Ask for the grading report, check that the report number laser-inscribed on the stone matches the report under a 10x loupe, and make sure the invoice names the stone. Some simple testers cannot tell moissanite from diamond, so the report and inscription are the reliable proof. We show you both in our showroom before you pay.

q: What does total carat weight mean on diamond earrings, a necklace or a bangle?
a: Total carat weight is the combined weight of all the diamonds in the piece, not the size of one stone. A pair of earrings marked 1 carat total, for example, has about half a carat in each earring. Our reports and invoices list the total weight, the number of diamonds and their quality.

q: Where is the BIS hallmark stamped on a ring, pendant, earring or bangle?
a: It is usually on the inside of a ring's band, on the back or the bail of a pendant, on the post or back of an earring, and on the inside of a bangle or kada. The mark has the BIS logo, the purity grade and a six-character HUID. We can show it to you under a loupe and match it to your bill.

q: How do I clean and store Polki and Kundan jewellery at home?
a: Wipe it gently with a soft dry cloth after wearing, keep it away from water, perfume and creams, and store each piece separately in a soft pouch or lined box. Do not soak it or rub the stones hard. Bring heavy sets to our showroom for professional cleaning.

q: Where in Surat can I see certified natural and lab-grown solitaires under a loupe before I buy?

q: Which diamond shape looks biggest and suits a small hand or short fingers?
a: Elongated shapes such as oval, pear and marquise usually look larger for their carat weight and make fingers look longer. A slim band also helps on smaller hands. The grading report confirms the shape, measurements and weight, and you can try several shapes at our showroom.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a gold, champagne or beige lehenga so it does not blend into the fabric?
a: Choose contrast rather than more gold: diamonds, or Polki set with emeralds, rubies or pearls, stand out clearly against zari. Pick one hero piece, usually the necklace, and repeat one stone colour in the earrings and tikka. Bring a photo of your lehenga to our Parle Point showroom and we will try pieces against it with you. q: Which jewellery set suits an engagement lehenga - a light Polki choker or a diamond collar necklace?
a: Both work: a light Polki choker suits a rich, traditional lehenga, while a diamond collar suits pastel, ivory or modern outfits and evening functions. Keep the engagement set lighter than the wedding set and choose pieces you can wear again. Every piece comes with its grading report and a BIS HUID hallmark on the gold. Read more: /blog/engagement-lehenga-jewellery-polki-choker-or-diamond-collar

q: What should I wear on my forehead and ears with a bridal veil or head dupatta?
a: A slim maang tikka in the centre parting, or a passa on one side, usually works best because both sit under or beside the drape without lifting it. Choose longer earrings to frame the face, and skip forehead jewellery if the veil has a heavy border. Bring your dupatta to our showroom to try the full look. Read more: /blog/maang-tikka-passa-or-nothing-with-a-bridal-veil

q: What jewellery can a groom wear with a sherwani?
a: Two or three pieces are enough: a pearl or Polki mala over the sherwani, one strong ring, and a kada or small diamond studs. Match the metal tone and one stone colour to the bride's set, and keep a brooch for the blazer at the reception. Gold pieces carry a BIS HUID hallmark and diamonds come with their grading report. Read more: /blog/what-jewellery-can-a-groom-wear-with-a-sherwani

q: What should I check when buying jewellery on Dhanteras or Diwali?
a: Check five things before you pay: the BIS hallmark on the gold, the 6-character HUID verified in the BIS Care app, an itemised bill with gold weight and stone details, the diamond grading report number (matched to the laser inscription on solitaires), and the exchange terms in writing. A good jeweller will happily let you check each one at the counter. WhatsApp +91 99980 43886 if you want us to keep pieces ready for you.

q: How can I check gold purity at home - are the magnet, acid or scratch tests reliable?
a: No, home tests are not reliable: a magnet only catches some obvious non-gold metals, and acid or scratch tests need training and can damage the piece. The dependable proof is the BIS hallmark with its HUID, which you can verify in the BIS Care app. For a precise reading, an XRF test at a BIS-recognised hallmarking centre measures purity without harming the jewellery. We show you the hallmark on every piece at our showroom.

q: Can I buy a loose certified diamond in Surat and have a ring made around it in a design I choose?
a: Yes. At Vaishnavi Jewels you choose a certified solitaire with its IGI, EGL or TGL report, match its laser-inscribed number under a loupe, then pick the setting, band and gold. We make the ring in our own manufacturing unit, usually in 2 to 4 weeks, and the gold mount is BIS HUID hallmarked. Read more: /blog/choose-a-certified-solitaire-and-design-your-own-ring-in-surat

q: What does fluorescence mean on a diamond certificate, and should it worry me?
a: Fluorescence is how a diamond glows, usually blue, under ultraviolet light, and reports grade it from None to Very Strong. In normal light most diamonds look the same whatever the grade; only occasionally can strong fluorescence make a stone look slightly hazy. The best check is to look at the stone yourself in daylight, which we are happy to do with you at the showroom.

q: What does eye-clean mean, and which clarity grade is enough for an everyday solitaire?
a: Eye-clean means you cannot see any inclusions with the naked eye at a normal viewing distance. Many VS and some SI stones are eye-clean, but it depends on the stone's size, shape and where the inclusions sit, so the grade alone does not decide it. Read the clarity plot on the report and look at the stone under a loupe and with your own eyes; we do this with you at the counter.

q: How can I find my partner's ring size secretly before buying an engagement ring?
a: Borrow a ring she already wears on the same finger and hand and have it measured, or trace its inside circle on paper. A close friend or family member can also find out her size casually. If the size is not exact, resizing is possible later and is charged on actuals, though rings with diamonds set all the way round are harder to resize.

q: Can I clean my diamond jewellery at home with soap, toothpaste or an ultrasonic cleaner?
a: Use warm water, a few drops of mild soap and a soft toothbrush, then rinse and dry with a lint-free cloth. Avoid toothpaste and other abrasives, which can scratch the gold, and avoid ultrasonic cleaners at home because the vibration can loosen stones; never use them on Polki or Kundan. Bring your jewellery to our showroom for a prong check and professional cleaning.
